concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 8 / research.md Statistical Methodology (permutation-FDR row)
concerns.text: The permutation-FDR step (FR-008) never specifies the permutation scheme. Under strong spatial autocorrelation (which the plan itself measures via Moran's I), naive i.i.d. permutation of the outcome breaks the spatial dependence structure and yields anti-conservative permutation p-values. Specify a spatially constrained permutation (e.g., block/toroidal shifts or permuting within spatial blocks) in correction.py, or justify the i.i.d. scheme.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 5 / research.md 'Effective sample size' row
concerns.text: N_eff = N/(1 + Moran's I) is a crude heuristic, not a standard effective-sample-size estimator (e.g., Clifford–Richardson / Dutilleul correction). It is acceptable as a reported descriptive quantity, but the plan should state it is a heuristic lower-bound-style adjustment and not use it to justify power claims; currently it 'feeds' the power caveat without qualification.

The Unexplained Variance Gap (0.68 − Observed_R²) is a difference against a spec-stated constant whose source is unverified (Zhou et al. 2020, flagged). The plan correctly labels it provisional, but the metric is scientifically meaningful only if the ceiling is empirically established for comparable predictors/resolution; the report should state that a negative gap (Observed_R² > 0.68) would indicate the ceiling is invalid, not that the model 'exceeds literature' — add this interpretation guard.
